items.prompt: Black to move. Tap the black pawn that protects the pawn on d5.

claims.statement: Exactly one black pawn (c6) attacks d5, so it protects it.
c6 holds the black pawn.

hints: Look for a pawn, not a piece.
A pawn protects a square diagonally in front of it, towards the enemy.
It stands on the file next to d5, one rank higher than d5.
items.explain: The c6 pawn protects d5 because a black pawn attacks the two squares diagonally ahead of it, b5 and d5. So no piece has to guard d5.

items.prompt: After the exchange on d5, which file holds no pawn of either colour?

claims.statement: The c-file holds no pawn of either colour.

hints: Count the files with no pawns on them.
The pawns that stood on the c-file have both left it.
It is the file next to the b-file and the d-file.
items.explain: White's c-pawn went to d5 and was captured; Black's c-pawn took it and stands on d5. Neither side has a pawn left on the c-file, so rooks can use it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap each black pawn that can attack d4 with a single move.

claims.statement: Exactly two pawn moves attack d4: c6-c5 and e6-e5.

hints: A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally ahead of it.
d4 is attacked from c5 and from e5.
Which black pawns can reach c5 or e5 in one step?
items.explain: A black pawn on c5 or e5 attacks d4. The c-pawn and the e-pawn can each get there in one move, so they are Black's two breaks against the centre.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is ...c5 within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move? Predict, then check.

answer.outcome: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best
options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...c5 is the engine's first choice.
d5 is empty, so c6 guards nothing.

hints: Look at d5. Is there a pawn there to guard?
Which white pawn does ...c5 attack?
The c6 pawn is free to move because d5 is empty.
items.explain: The d5 pawn is gone, so the c6 pawn has no guarding job. ...c5 attacks d4, the pawn White needs in front of e4, and at depth 16 it is the engine's first choice. [I] Development matters too: the pair is a rule of thumb, not a controlled test.
options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

items.prompt: Black to move. Is ...c5 within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move? Predict, then check.

options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

claims.statement: Now c6 is the only black pawn that protects d5.
At depth 16 ...c5 is more than 0.4 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: Look at d5. What protects it now?
If the c-pawn leaves, which black pieces still guard d5?
White can capture on d5 or on c5 and gain time.
items.explain: Here d5 still stands and c6 is its only pawn guard; the e-pawn has not moved. ...c5 leaves d5 to the knight and queen, and at depth 16 it is more than 0.4 pawn worse than the best move. This position is also far less developed than the first, so read the pair as a rule of thumb [I]: check who guards d5 before the c-pawn leaves.
options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

items.prompt: Black to move. Is ...c5 within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move? Predict, then check. (One thing differs from the first position: the white h-pawn stands on h3.)

answer.outcome: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best
options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

claims.statement: The white pawn stands on h3.
At depth 16 ...c5 is still the engine's first choice.

hints: Compare with the first position: what is different?
Does the h-pawn change what ...c5 attacks?
d5 is still empty and d4 still stands.
items.explain: The h-pawn has no part in the fight over d4, so the answer does not change. A feature that does not touch the break does not matter.
options: Yes, ...c5 is within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best

items.prompt: White to move. Black has pawns on d5 and e5 and the c-file is open. Which pawn move attacks d5 from the side?

claims.statement: After e4 one white pawn attacks d5.
At depth 16 e4 is the engine's first choice.
At depth 16 dxe5 is at least 0.25 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: Which white pawn can move to a square next to d5?
It stands on e3 and has a free square in front of it.
The pawn goes to e4.
items.explain: The e-pawn on e3 moves to e4, where it attacks d5. The knight on c3, the bishop on d3 and the queen stand ready to recapture there, and at depth 16 it is the engine's first choice.

feedback_by_move.d4e5: dxe5 trades the d-pawn for the e-pawn but gives up the tension. At depth 16 it is at least 0.25 pawn below e4.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's queen attacks the b7 pawn. Which moves defend it and keep the position balanced?

claims.statement: b7 is the only loose black unit.
At depth 16 Qc7, Qb6 and Qc8 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 Nbd7 is at least 0.5 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: What does the queen on b3 attack that nothing defends?
Which black piece can protect b7?
The queen can protect b7 from c7, b6 or c8.
items.explain: The queen on d8 can protect b7 from three squares. At depth 16 all three are within 0.4 pawn of the best move, so Black does not have to give up the bishop plan.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: Nbd7 ignores the threat: Qxb7 wins the pawn, and at depth 16 the move is at least 0.5 pawn worse than the best.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on h4 attacks the bishop. Which retreats keep the bishop outside the chain and stay within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best?

claims.statement: One white piece (the knight on h4) attacks f5.
At depth 16 Bg6 and Be4 are both within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Which white piece attacks f5?
The bishop can retreat along the same diagonal in two directions.
Both ends of the diagonal, g6 and e4, are playable.
items.explain: The bishop stays on its own diagonal and out of the pawn chain. Masters chose ...Be4 in 635 games and ...Bg6 in 522, and at depth 16 both are within 0.4 pawn of the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Qe7, e5 and Re8 are within 0.3 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: What does your opponent's last move attack?
Which pawn moves change the structure?
Check the pawn you want to move: is it guarding something that matters?
items.explain: Several moves are fine at depth 16: ...e5 is the break of this lesson, and ...Qe7 and ...Re8 prepare it. ...c5 is a little worse here.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a sound move that develops the light-squared bishop.

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...Bf5 and ...Bg4 are within 0.15 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Look at your light-squared bishop.
Which of its diagonals is still open?
Look at f5 and g4.
items.explain: Both bishop moves keep the c8 bishop outside the chain, and at depth 16 both are within 0.15 pawn of the best move. ...e6 is sound too (about 0.02 pawn behind), but it shuts the bishop in, the price the lesson showed.

items.prompt: White to move. Which pawn move attacks d5 from the side, a break that the knights and the bishop can support?

claims.statement: At depth 16 e4 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which pawn can step to a square next to d5?
The pieces behind the pawn can recapture.
Look at e4.
items.explain: e4 opens the centre with the knights and the bishop ready to recapture, and at depth 16 it is the engine's first choice. Other moves develop or wait; the break is playable because the pieces are ready.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Qc2, Bd3, Be2, a3 and h3 are within 0.25 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Which pieces are still at home?
Is any break urgent right now?
Develop and keep d4 and c4 protected.
items.explain: A break is possible but not needed yet: the useful moves develop a piece or make a waiting move. At depth 16 five such moves are within 0.25 pawn of the best, so a break is not the answer to every position.
